(1) the ED lexical texts are not a uniform group; (2) they are not all copied in the same manner; (3) they are not copied by the same people; (4) they are copied by scribes with a variety of educational backgrounds; (5) the texts are copied for various purposes; (6) they are copied in a variety of contexts, and (7) their copying is not always a matter of simple transmission.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these texts are a window into the world of the Old Babylonian scholar, who, while he might be aware of his own place in history, was nevertheless deeply immersed in the past.
the Old Babylonian ED lexical texts are the guardians of tradition, and that they are a significant and unique source for the study of Old Babylonian cuneiform writing and its transmission.

the ED lexical texts in Old Babylonian copies represent a unique phenomenon in the history of cuneiform writing: they are the only surviving examples of the use of writing for the purpose of preserving ancient traditions, and they were copied for that purpose for more than one thousand years, until the time when the tradition itself was no longer viable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the Old Babylonian lexical tradition was a living, dynamic, tradition that was constantly changing.
the lexical corpus in the early Old Babylonican period was not a single tradition but a conglomeration of traditions that were not always compatible with each other.
the ED texts in Old Babylonian copies are a significant but hitherto neglected part of the cuneifonn lexical corpus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Old Babylonian scribal schools were not only interested in copying the ED lexical texts for their own sake but that they also used them to create new compositions.
the Old Babylonian lexical tradition was not just a continuation of the Early Dynatic tradition, but that the latter had a significant role to play in the former.
the ED lexical corpus was not a mere fossil of an earlier age.
